newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LINDROS ADDS DISCIPLINE TO HIS REPERTOIRE.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LINDROS ADDS DISCIPLINE TO HIS REPERTOIRE.

text.p: Eric Lindros scored three times for his Philadelphia Flyers in Game 3 of the NHL Eastern Conference finals but it was his restraint and discipline that really impressed his coach on Tuesday.
"I think he showed tonight the kind of great player he is," said Philadelphia coach Terry Murray after a 6-3 win that gave his team a 2-1 lead in the best-of-seven series.
"The biggest thing he did was show the discipline, the patience and the poise," Murray said of Lindros's willingness to turn the other cheek at times.
"That was very important for our captain to show."
It has been an ill-tempered series with players on both teams commiting offences that would land them in jail had they taken place on the streets of New York -- or even Philadelphia.
And Lindros may be the most talented thug in the National Hockey League these days, using his stick and great physical strength to do more than just score goals.

The Rangers took exception to the way Lindros tried to re-arrange Doug Lidster's nose with his stick in Game 1, not to mention a number of other vicious hits, including lifting Luc Robitaille and slamming him to the ice on his head.
So they ganged up on Lindros in Game 2, punishing him at every opportunity.
That Lindros was able to avoid the temptation for revenge Tuesday impressed coach Murray.

"I think after Game Two there was a reason for him to come back and do some stuff that might have been a bit over the line as far as hitting late or retailiating to what happened at the end of Game Two.
"He took a lot of abuse in Game 2."
Happy as he was with Lindros's restraint, Murray is not about to rein in his most explosive weapon.
"He's a big guy that's going to answer the bell. He's going to get his opportunities to do his stuff.
"He's going to play on the edge, that's fine, he's that kind of player and I'm not going to try to take that away from his game," Murray said of his maturing young star.

"But I think the key is that you don't step over the edge ... so that you're going to put the team in trouble all night long and that's what he showed tonight," Murray said of Lindros, who has been known to leave "the edge" well back in his rear view mirror on occasion.
"You have to use common sense and good judgment in your game," Murray said.

Lindros single-handedly made the game's first goal happen when he drove to the right side of the Rangers' net, bringing goaltender Mike Richter off his feet before powering around the back of the net and stuffing the puck in the other side.
"It was a great play. Lindros was real strong on the puck coming around the net," Murray said.

Lindros added his eighth goal of the post-season at a crucial time -- just after the Rangers had tied the game 2-2 -- blasting the puck past Richter after receiving a perfect pass from Legion of Doom linemate John LeClair.
And he created general havoc in front of the New York goal all night before putting an exclamation point on the victory with an empty netter in the final minute.
"Great players make great plays," LeClair said. "Lindros dominated the game.
"And when they tied it, Eric took control of the game, that's what great players do."
But sometimes it's what you don't do that makes head coaches sleep easier.
